principles.title: Identity is maintained coherence
principles.statement: Identity is the maintained relationship among purpose, boundaries, memory, permissions, and action across changing contexts.

principles.title: Self and substrate are distinct
principles.statement: Intention and policy belong to the IAM product layer; execution belongs to a separate substrate reached through an explicit interface.

principles.title: Capability is granted, not assumed
principles.statement: Power should be explicit, bounded, reviewable, and limited to what a role requires.

principles.title: Composition creates relationship
principles.statement: Complex behavior emerges through bounded units, visible inputs and outputs, and inspectable transformations.

principles.title: Memory is accountable continuity
principles.statement: Memory joins identifiable structure to changing state and recoverable sequence; it is stewardship of continuity rather than a metaphysical identity claim.

principles.title: Evidence preserves transformation
principles.statement: Trustworthy accounts preserve what changed, in what order, and under which explicit conditions and capabilities.

principles.title: Recursion is bounded return
principles.statement: Return is responsible when prior state, external conditions, and continuation boundaries are preserved or explicitly declared missing.

principles.title: Meaning does not override evidence
principles.statement: Mythic language may orient values and interpretation, while contracts, evidence, policy, and explicit grants govern operations.

principles.title: Boundaries enable exploration
principles.statement: Safe experimentation depends on bounded environments where learning can occur without silently inheriting unrestricted power.
